clue.text: Adopt a noncommittal attitude to burden engulfing trustee

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the first word wraps itself around the second

blocks.note: to saddle someone is to burden them
TR is a dictionary abbreviation for trustee

explanation.surface: Someone stays neutral about a dispute that is weighing down a trustee.
explanation.walkthrough: To straddle an issue is to sit on the fence, keeping a foot on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Straddling a question means favouring neither side, which is exactly sitting on the fence about it.

clue.text: Flowers in competition provided by yours truly

blocks.note: a race is a competition
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: A flower show entry where the speaker supplied the blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: A raceme is a botanical term for a flower cluster, such as a foxglove spike, so the plural clue word is fair for one cluster of many flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is an unbranched stalk bearing many individual blooms along its length, a botanical cluster.

clue.text: Bug – one seen in green soup!

indicators.note: a soup is a mess or jumble, so the colour word is stirred into a new order
something seen in a thing sits inside it, so the single letter goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A diner finds an insect floating in pea soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Bug looks like the insect in the soup, but it is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate them, and enrage is a stronger form of the same verb.

clue.text: 6 on a roll collects nothing for player

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sitting on another simply comes first
collecting something means gathering it in, so the empty symbol is taken inside

blocks.note: VI is the Roman numeral six
O looks like zero
a roll is a list, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Someone on a lucky streak at dice keeps scoring zero, a confusing gambling scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is just the number, written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A violist is someone who plays the viola, so a performing musician in an orchestra.

clue.text: After liberation, Fisher rises to give some words

indicators.note: after places the animal's letters behind the abbreviation
in a down answer rising means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: Lib is short for liberation, as in women's lib
an otter catches fish

explanation.surface: After being freed, a man named Fisher stands up to make a short speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Fisher looks like a surname, but it is any creature that fishes. A libretto is the text of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The libretto is the written text of an opera or musical, so the words set to its music.

clue.text: Merlot I'd decanted into Methuselah?

indicators.note: wine that is decanted is poured out and moved, so these letters are shifted around

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pouring red wine into a methuselah, the giant champagne bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: A methuselah is a huge wine bottle, which suits the decanting, but here it is the biblical patriarch who lived 969 years; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah, the longest-lived man in the Bible, is the ultimate example of a veteran or elderly person.

clue.text: Prime self-contained house on the outskirts of Oakhill

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters of the village name are kept
one thing on another in a down answer comes first, so the pieces join in order

blocks.note: s/c is the estate agents' abbreviation for self-contained
HO is an abbreviation for house
first and last letters of the place name

explanation.surface: An estate agent's advert for a prime self-contained house near a village.
explanation.walkthrough: Prime reads as an estate agent's adjective, but it is the verb meaning to prepare someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To prime someone is to coach or train them in advance, and to school means the same verb.

clue.text: Accomplish the removal of rights without revolutionary communist

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the political word is turned back to front
without means lacking, so those letters are taken away from the legal word

blocks.note: attainder was the old legal forfeiture of civil rights after a conviction for treason
red is the colour of communism

explanation.surface: A political purge that strips people of their rights, apart from one radical.
explanation.walkthrough: Attainder is an archaic legal term; its last three letters are the communist read backwards, which are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to reach or achieve it, so a direct synonym for accomplishing it.

clue.text: Fool describing endless lust in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: with no end, the desire word loses its last letter
to describe in the old geometric sense is to draw a line around, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: an idiot is a fool
to lech is to lust

explanation.surface: A fool goes on about his endless lust in a rambling way.
explanation.walkthrough: An idiolect is the speech habits peculiar to one person.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiolect is one individual's particular way of using language, their personal manner of speaking.

clue.text: Vulgar party game

blocks.note: base means low or vulgar
a ball is a formal party

explanation.surface: A crude party game, the sort played late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Vulgar party game reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces and a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is the American bat-and-ball sport, so a straightforward example of a game.

clue.text: Legal reasons for numberless allowances

indicators.note: the suffix -less means lacking, so the word for allowances goes without the abbreviation named in front of it

blocks.note: rations are fixed allowances of food
N is short for number

explanation.surface: A court explaining why some allowances are not numbered.
explanation.walkthrough: Numberless looks like a single word meaning countless; split it, and the abbreviation for number goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio, short for ratio decidendi, is the legal principle underpinning a court judgment, the reasoning behind it.

clue.text: Ego's endless turmoil resulting in lethargy

indicators.note: turmoil is confusion and upheaval, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the ego is the self, I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's inner turmoil leaves them listless and unmotivated.
explanation.walkthrough: Endless looks like the usual signal to drop a last letter; here it is the anagram fodder itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness and lethargy both name a state of inactivity and sluggishness, a lack of energy.

clue.text: Disorder revealed by septum bleeding

indicators.note: revealed by means shown by the words that follow, so the letters sit in plain view across them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A medical condition shown by a nosebleed from the septum.
explanation.walkthrough: Disorder sounds medical in this setting, but it means a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumble is a confused or untidy heap, so a state of disorder, as in hair in a tumble.

clue.text: Happy to welcome Basque separatists' women – I don't believe you!

indicators.note: welcoming guests means taking them in, so the outer word holds the others

blocks.note: gay in its older sense of merry
ETA was the Basque separatist group
W is short for women

explanation.surface: A pleased host greets wives of Basque militants, then someone scoffs in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: Get away is an exclamation of disbelief, much like you're joking.
explanation.definitionFit: Get away! is an informal exclamation expressing surprise or doubt at what someone has said.

clue.text: One may contribute coyly to a four-letter word

definitions.text: One may contribute coyly to a four-letter word

blocks.clueFragment: One may contribute coyly to a four-letter word
blocks.note: surface reading: someone shyly helping to build a short word

blocks.clueFragment: contribute coyly to a four-letter word
blocks.note: setter's reading: a printed star stands in for a letter of a swear word, so it is printed politely

explanation.walkthrough: Four-letter word here means a swear word, and printing it with stars in place of letters is a coy way to avoid spelling it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers replace letters of obscenities with this star symbol, so it forms part of the censored swearword.

clue.text: Advocate attending unfashionable game in America

indicators.note: the prefix un- undoes what follows, so the stylish letter is taken away from the game rather than added

blocks.note: attending a play is being at it
tourney is the American word for a tournament
U means upper class, hence fashionable

explanation.surface: A lawyer goes to an outdated sports match while in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class, so fashionable, is a crossword convention; un-fashionable drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: In America an attorney is a lawyer who represents clients in court, so an advocate.

clue.text: Immoral bishop's high during function

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the first pieces go inside the function

blocks.note: Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
up means high
cot is short for cotangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A bishop is drunk or stoned at an official function, a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: High and function suggest a bishop drunk at a party; function is the maths kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone corrupt is dishonest and morally rotten, so the adjective matches immoral closely.

clue.text: Allot OAP accommodation in Californian city

indicators.note: accommodation implies adjusting or fitting things in, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A council housing a pensioner in sunny California.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAP is an old-age pensioner in Britain. Palo Alto is the Silicon Valley city next to Stanford.
explanation.definitionFit: Palo Alto is a city in the San Francisco Bay Area of California, home to Stanford University.

clue.text: Key involved in opening up protective cover

indicators.note: in a down answer going up means reading bottom to top, so the word is turned around
something involved in a thing is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: the outset is the opening of something
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A key is used to open up a protective casing.
explanation.walkthrough: A testudo was the Roman shield formation, soldiers locking shields overhead like a tortoise shell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman testudo, from the Latin for tortoise, was a roof of overlapping shields protecting troops.

clue.text: Flier for Cambridge University describing the origin of time

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only its first letter counts
to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the university surrounds the single letter

blocks.note: for and to are interchangeable in phrases like a letter to or for someone
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts
first letter

explanation.surface: A pilot flying for Cambridge University and talking about how time began.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University points to the English one; it is the other Cambridge, in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomtit is a small bird, usually a blue tit, so a creature that flies.

clue.text: Oilmen regularly discover short form of hydrocarbon

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the workers' word is taken
short means cut off, so the verb loses its final letter

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters
to find something is to discover it

explanation.surface: Oil workers routinely strike a quick source of hydrocarbons.
explanation.walkthrough: Short form looks like an abbreviation signal; short belongs to the wordplay and form of to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An olefin, also called an alkene, is a class of hydrocarbon with a carbon double bond.

clue.text: Encourages magazine to get rid of old type of paper

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so that letter is dropped from the magazine title

blocks.note: eggs on means encourages
Hello! is a British celebrity magazine
O is short for old

explanation.surface: Someone urges a magazine to stop using an outdated paper stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity gossip magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell paper is a kind of paper with a slightly rough finish like the surface of an egg.

clue.text: Those present get a bit of upside-down cake

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter

blocks.note: the gate is the number of spectators attending a match
taken as written
first letter

explanation.surface: Guests at a party are each given a slice of pineapple upside-down cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Upside-down cake reads as one item, but the cake is the definition alone. The gate is the crowd at a sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, from the French word for cake.

clue.text: Old comic's tip on film

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: a horn is a pointed tip, as of an anvil or a crescent moon
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A veteran comedian gives advice about a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Old comic suggests a retired comedian; it is The Hornet, a British boys' comic paper of the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hornet was a British weekly boys' story paper published by DC Thomson from 1963 to 1976.

clue.text: Football pundit biting the head off listener?

indicators.note: with its head bitten off, the name loses its first letter

blocks.note: Alan Shearer, former England striker and BBC football pundit

explanation.surface: A TV football pundit loses his temper and snaps at a viewer.
explanation.walkthrough: Biting someone's head off means snapping angrily at them, but here it removes a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearer is one who hears, so anyone listening; the question mark admits it is a little unusual.

clue.text: Lesson of Irish rock group heard to be in hardship

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the band's name is spoken, not how it is written
to be in something is to sit inside it, so these letters go within the word for hardship

blocks.note: U2 is the Irish rock band
a trial is a hardship or ordeal

explanation.surface: A lesson about an Irish band that fell on hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: The band's name is spoken as you two, spelt here U plus TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a teaching session with a tutor, so a lesson given to a small group.

clue.text: Relative velocity of a Perseid shower

indicators.note: a shower scatters things widely, so the letters fall in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The speed of meteors in the Perseid shower, measured relative to Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Perseids are an August meteor shower, so shower looks part of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspeed is an aircraft's speed measured relative to the surrounding air, not the ground.

clue.text: A Roman goddess in sacred texts

blocks.note: taken as written
Vesta was the Roman goddess of the hearth

explanation.surface: A Roman goddess appears in holy scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: The Avesta is the scripture of Zoroastrianism.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the collected body of Zoroastrian scriptures, so a set of holy writings.
